title: regional-gateway-harmonized-failover-and-streaming-protection
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a regional gateway failover and traffic harmonization strategy that preserves SLOs for latency (p50/p95) and availability while protecting long-lived streaming sessions. This ticket defines thresholds and mechanics for circuit breakers, load-shedding, sticky-session reconciliation, and traffic redistribution across regions/gateways.

Background: Our hosted API is globally fronted by regional gateways. We currently have per-region autoscaling and fallbacks, but lack a coordinated active-active traffic harmonization strategy that: 1) prevents cascading resource exhaustion during regional degradation, 2) gracefully sheds load for non-critical routes, and 3) preserves user experience for streaming/chat sessions where possible.

Scope: Engineering work to: define SLO targets by route class, codify circuit-breaker thresholds and state transitions, implement coordinated load-shedding policies in the gateway control plane, add session-safe failover paths for streaming (including KV-cache reconcilers and resume tokens), and build the rollout/canary plan with dashboards and runbooks.

Out of scope: Complete redesign of regional routing mesh or changes to customer-facing API semantics (we will rely on standard HTTP/2 streaming and resume tokens).
acceptance_criteria: SLOs defined and documented for route classes: control (auth), inference-sync (short-gen), inference-stream (long-stream), embeddings
Circuit-breaker rules implemented and tested: open at 5xx rate > 2% for 3m or p95 latency > 1000ms for 2m, half-open probing with backoff
Load-shedding policy implemented for non-critical routes (best-effort batching disabled, 429 with retry-after) and feature-flagged
Streaming session resume flow validated end-to-end (resume token + KV cache reconciliation) across region failover in staging
Automated canary shifts able to move 5-50% of traffic between regions with health checks and rollback on SLO regression
Runbook created with clear escalation and manual traffic-shift steps and postmortem template

runbook: Pre-failover checklist: ensure canary config is ready, alerting channels (SRE Slack #ha-alerts), and on-call roster assigned
Step 1: Enable canary shift to target region at 5% using feature flag 'gateway.harmonized_canary'
Step 2: Observe p50/p95 latency and 5xx rate on the canary for 10 minutes; if any SLO metric regresses beyond threshold, abort and rollback flag
Step 3: If canary healthy, increment to 25% for 15 minutes and re-evaluate; then 50% and full if stable
Manual rollback: disable flag and reroute via control-plane to original region; run cache-clearing jobs if sticky session mismatches observed
Emergency: If upstream region crashes and circuit-breakers trip across multiple edge nodes, trigger 'global-failover' playbook and engage network ops
testing_plan: Unit tests for circuit-breaker transitions and backoff timings
Chaos test: induce increased p95 latency in region A and validate automatic shedding and healthy-region routing in staging
Streaming resilience test: simulate TCP/HTTP2 disconnects and verify resume-token + KV reconciliation for 100 concurrent sessions
Load test: ramp best-effort embedding requests to verify 429-based shedding and retry-after header behavior
Canary automation: scripted traffic shift with synthetic probes and SLO-based halt conditions
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Cold KV cache after failover could cause increased latencies for resumed streams. Mitigation: prioritized cache warmup for sessions that failed over and a 'cold-warm' latency budget in SLOs.
Risk: Overaggressive shedding could cause customer-visible 429s. Mitigation: tiered shedding with user-tier aware rules (enterprise routes exempt until last-resort).
Risk: Flapping between half-open and open states under noisy signals. Mitigation: hysteresis (longer windows for recovery) and quorum-based health across gateway fleet.
Risk: Rollout coordination errors. Mitigation: single-point rollout controller with audit logs and automated rollback triggers tied to SLO dashboards.
implementation_notes: Gateway will expose metrics: gateway.circuit_state, gateway.open_count, gateway.shed_rate, gateway.resume_success_rate
Introduce new feature flag namespace gateway.harmonized.* to control canary and shedding behavior per-customer and per-route-class
Streaming resumes use a two-phase handshake: client resume token -> gateway validation -> backend KV reconciliation -> client resume ack
Prefer 429+Retry-After for load-shedding non-critical routes; use 503 for short-term global overload where retry semantics are different
All changes must include integration tests that run against staging multi-region deployment (us-east, eu-west)
